prerequisites: Having studied Physics in the last year of high school (2º de bachillerato)
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed systems of ideal gases.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the subject.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical quantities. Treatment of measurement errors.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First principle of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing
Analysis of results and preparation of practice reports
Solving problems and preparing practice reports, assignments, etc.
assessment_rules: The final grade NFO is calculated using the formula NFO = EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment grade and CGO is the global exam grade. A minimum of 3.5 points (out of 10) is required in the global exam to combine with continuous assessment. A minimum global score of 2.0 points out of 5.5 is required for continuous assessment; otherwise, continuous assessment is scored zero. Any final score below 5.0 points will result in a FAIL. Extraordinary calls follow the same rules, with continuous assessment scores remaining valid.
